rules.quote: Never mix ‘from’ or ‘between’ with an en dash.

rules.quote: For financial years, use 4 digits for the first number and only 2 digits for the second. Join them with an unspaced en dash.

rules.quote: If one part of a coordinate noun is made up of more than one word, use a space either side of the en dash. Otherwise, do not include spaces around en dashes for coordinate nouns.
rules.violation_condition: a coordinate noun joining single words with spaces around the en dash, or joining a multi-word part without spaces around the en dash
when: When joining coordinate nouns with an en dash.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Captures the formation and spacing rules for coordinate nouns.

covers.quote: Spaced en dashes are Australian government style and should be used in digital content.

examples.note: Spaced en dashes setting off parenthetical information.

parts.quote: Three rivers – the Murray, Darling and Murrumbidgee – were discussed in the report.

rules.quote: Always space punctuating en dashes with a single space on either side of the dash.
rules.violation_condition: a punctuating en dash used in a sentence to set off parenthetical or non-essential information without spaces on both sides
when: When using an en dash inside a sentence to set off non-essential or parenthetical information.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Specific spacing requirement for parenthetical en dashes.

covers.quote: If you remove the content between the en dashes, the rest of the sentence must be a complete sentence.

examples.note: The right side is a complete sentence.

parts.quote: Solar, wind, hydro and tidal power – all are viable options for renewable energy.

examples.note: Neither side of the single dash forms a complete sentence.

parts.quote: Solar, wind, hydro and tidal power – are viable options for renewable energy.

rules.quote: In a sentence with one en dash, one side of the dash must be a complete sentence.
rules.violation_condition: a sentence with a single punctuating en dash where neither side forms a complete sentence
when: When using a single en dash to introduce or conclude parenthetical information.
rules.why: G-2, E-2: Grammatical completeness rule for single en dash constructions.

rules.quote: If you are using em dashes in your content, don’t space them.
rules.violation_condition: an em dash with spaces on either side
when: When em dashes are used in text (e.g. per an external publisher's style).
rules.why: G-2: Explicit prohibition against spaced em dashes.

covers.quote: To show a sudden interruption in quotations and reported speech, use 2 em dashes in a row. The 2 em dashes follow a space.
Two em dashes also show when a name or other information is omitted in body text in general content.

examples.note: Space used when replacing a whole word.

parts.quote: The deed, signed by ——, was legally binding.

examples.note: No space between letter and em dashes when replacing part of a word.

parts.quote: S—— signed the deed in 2017.

rules.quote: Use a space if the em dashes replace a whole word, but don’t include a space between the dashes and part of the word.
rules.violation_condition: two em dashes used for omissions with incorrect spacing (either lacking space when replacing a whole word, or including a space when replacing part of a word)
when: When using two em dashes to show deliberate omissions of words or parts of words.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Consolidates rules and spacing for double em dashes used for omissions/interruptions.
